method_findings.repeat_swap_then_prune_005-n32: Across the saved 19,435 sites, guided pruning shortens 13,301 (68.438%) and lowers mean bullets from 3.99372 to 2.91057; its mean reconstruction-score loss is 0.00260569 versus 0.01061195 for deterministic random deletion from the same repeated-swaps parent. Per-cell retained bullet counts are identical, but token lengths are not matched, and smaller reconstruction loss does not prove semantic superiority. In analysis/final-v1.json, native full-question counts are 38/100 for Multihop (multi-token), 53/120 for Chained intermediates, and 84/100 for Role-bound association, versus parent counts 41/100, 51/120, and 84/100; Hallucination (chat) has 2472/5557 contradictions versus 2615/5552 in the parent, with nearly identical count-matched random error rate. Selected cases show some helpful deletion of unsupported names, but also complete-bridge losses and verdict changes that preserve the flagged content or directional relation; shared gains must not be credited uniquely to the guided rule. All four saved paired guided-versus-random native confidence intervals include zero, and the previously observed banks and outcome-selected examples support exploratory interpretation rather than prevalence or fresh confirmation.
method_findings.repeated_swaps_random_delete_match_005-n: This deterministic control deletes from the same repeated-swaps parent to match the guided retained bullet count at every cell, not exact token length; its mean 2.91057 bullets and 68.438% shortened sites are therefore identical, while its mean reconstruction-score loss is larger. In analysis/final-v1.json, native full-question counts are 36/100 for Multihop (multi-token), 51/120 for Chained intermediates, and 84/100 for Role-bound association, with Hallucination (chat) at 2471/5552 contradictions, so the guided hallucination reduction is also obtained by random shortening. The shared chain gain exposes an already-present numeral to the scored extraction, whereas Brancusi and reverse-direction hairdresser losses physically remove essential bridge or binding evidence; other scored losses retain the relevant sentence and reveal judgment sensitivity. Two unchanged examples across these partitions have metadata-only retained-evidence differences, and none has an identical-text scored-verdict flip. The full native paired guided-versus-random intervals all include zero; this outcome-selected review does not estimate frequency, validate all prose, or establish a new held-out result.
